actions: Wire the existing LB-010 RecoveryController into the single DesktopLifecycle-owned production runtime through one stoppable watchdog

Expose a nonblocking liveness read for the actual CodingToolsRuntime already owned behind the PEP so MCP/PEP/Tunnel post-Ready failures can be classified without a second runtime or PID-only ownership
records.reason: The formal G2 generation 3 independent adversarial review found that the accepted LB-010 RecoveryController had no production recover_auto/observe_stable_ready caller and no post-Ready MCP/PEP/Tunnel watchdog. The production runtime is owned in app/background.rs and the actual CodingToolsRuntime is intentionally encapsulated behind the PEP, so these adjacent seams are the minimum required composition points.
records.evidence_ref: G2 generation 3 review provenance commit 863a197fe20b5e6735aa7bdc847181f66e26df8d plus current source search showing no production recover_auto/observe_stable_ready caller before this repair.

actions: Add cooperative cancellation and bounded recovery-readiness probes required to interrupt an automatic recovery attempt
Decouple DesktopLifecycle runtime snapshot reads and explicit-control cancellation from the recovery runtime-owner lock without changing policy, raw MCP, secret, or process-ownership semantics
records.reason: The formal G2 generation 4 independent adversarial review found that production automatic recovery held DesktopLifecycle synchronization across retry backoff and readiness, blocking snapshots and explicit controls. The current MCP readiness HTTP request can block for about two seconds and a Tunnel readiness health probe can issue two such requests, so a cancellation token alone cannot satisfy the frozen user-control interruption contract without narrowly bounded recovery-only transport seams.
records.evidence_ref: G2 generation 4 review provenance commit d2d4e990faf6841c12033d5f223c4bbae1a036bd plus current src-tauri/src/mcp/http.rs and src-tauri/src/tunnel/health.rs timeout implementations inspected before this repair.

actions: Add the deterministic DesktopLifecycle concurrency regression that deliberately holds the watchdog runtime owner while verifying cached runtime_snapshot responsiveness and explicit-control recovery cancellation before lifecycle lock acquisition
records.reason: The formal G2 generation 4 independent adversarial review found that automatic recovery could block runtime snapshots and explicit manual controls. The production synchronization seam is owned by DesktopLifecycle in app/background.rs, so proving the repair dynamically requires one adjacent background integration test outside LB-010's normal recovery test path.
records.evidence_ref: G2 generation 4 review provenance commit d2d4e990faf6841c12033d5f223c4bbae1a036bd and tests/integration/background/background.rs::explicit_control_cancels_before_owner_lock_and_snapshot_remains_responsive

actions: Route production AutoRecoveryRuntime permission-mode changes through the control-aware recovery reconciliation path so a permission change that cancels in-flight automatic recovery resumes the same outage generation and attempt instead of leaving Faulted(UserStopped)
records.reason: The formal G2 generation 5 independent adversarial review found that DesktopLifecycle permission changes cancel automatic recovery before taking the lifecycle lock, while the AutoRecoveryRuntime ExitRuntime adapter previously forwarded the mode change directly to RuntimeOrchestrator and could leave the cancelled recovery terminalized as Faulted(UserStopped). background.rs is the minimum adjacent production composition seam outside LB-010 writable paths.
records.evidence_ref: G2 generation 5 review provenance commit b456e223a8d5d25f879a05b2928ab30a1611d3f0 plus the production AutoRecoveryRuntime ExitRuntime permission-mode adapter in src-tauri/src/app/background.rs
